facts.fact: It was built in Brabantine late-Gothic style between 1439 and 1469 and is famous for its lace-like detail.
facts.quote: Built in a Brabantine late-Gothic style between 1439 and 1469, it is famous for its ornate architecture, crafted in lace-like detail.

facts.fact: The first architect, Sulpitius Van Vorst, died early and was followed briefly by Jan Keldermans II, who died in 1445.
facts.quote: The first architect, Sulpitius Van Vorst, died soon after the rear wings of the complex got started and was succeeded briefly by Jan Keldermans II, whose death in 1445 ended the first construction campaign.

facts.fact: Work resumed in 1448 under Matheus de Layens.
facts.quote: The project resumed in 1448 under the direction of Matheus de Layens.

facts.fact: The first plans, influenced by Brussels Town Hall, had a corner belfry; de Layens changed this to today's symmetrical turrets.
facts.quote: The initial plans, influenced by Brussels' Town Hall, included a belfry tower at one of the corners. This design was modified by de Layens, resulting in the symmetrical arrangement of turrets observed today.

facts.fact: Above three storeys of pointed Gothic windows rise a parapet gallery and a steep roof with four tiers of dormers.
facts.quote: The Town Hall has three main stories, lined with pointed Gothic windows on the three sides visible from the Grote Markt. Above is a gallery parapet, behind which rises a steep roof studded with four tiers of dormers.

facts.fact: Its 236 statues in canopied niches date from after 1850, though the niches and carved corbels are original.
facts.quote: While the niches and corbels are original with the building, the 236 statues themselves are relatively recent, dating from after 1850.

facts.fact: A bomb in World War II damaged it, and repairs were only finished in 1983.
facts.quote: In World War II, a bomb strike in front of the building caused yet more damage; it took until 1983 before repairs were completed.

facts.fact: It was first built to showcase King Leopold II's Congo Free State at the 1897 International Exposition.
facts.quote: It was originally built to showcase King Leopold II's Congo Free State in the International Exposition of 1897.

facts.fact: The new museum was begun in 1904 to designs by Charles Girault, in a neoclassical palace style recalling the Petit Palais in Paris.
facts.quote: The new museum started construction in 1904 and was designed by the French architect Charles Girault in neoclassical "palace" architecture, reminiscent of the Petit Palais in Paris, with large gardens extending into the Tervuren Forest (a part of the Sonian Forest).

facts.fact: King Albert I opened it in 1910 as the Museum of the Belgian Congo.
facts.quote: It was officially opened in 1910, a year after the death of Leopold II, by his successor, King Albert I, and named the Museum of the Belgian Congo (French: Musée du Congo Belge, Dutch: Museum van Belgisch-Kongo).

facts.fact: The main building is 125 m long and 75 m wide.
facts.quote: The building is 125 metres (410 ft) long and 75 metres (246 ft) wide.

facts.fact: The renovation and extension plan was entrusted to Stéphane Beel Architects.
facts.quote: The Belgian Buildings Agency entrusted the plan to the Temporary Association Stéphane Beel Architects (TV SBA).

facts.fact: A new reception pavilion built in 2016 serves as the entrance.
facts.quote: A reception pavilion, newly built in 2016, between the management building and the Palace of Africa, functions as the entrance building.

facts.fact: It reopened as the AfricaMuseum on 9 December 2018.
facts.quote: Renamed AfricaMuseum, the museum was reopened on 9 December 2018.

facts.fact: The Grand Théâtre is Luxembourg City's main venue for drama, opera and ballet, opened in 1964 as the Théâtre Municipal.
facts.quote: The Grand Théâtre de Luxembourg, inaugurated in 1964 as the Théâtre Municipal de la Ville de Luxembourg is the city's major venue for drama, opera and ballet.

facts.fact: Parisian architect Alain Bourbonnais won the design competition.
facts.quote: The winner was Alain Bourbonnais (1925–1988), a Parisian architect.

facts.fact: Work began in autumn 1959 and the theatre opened on 15 April 1964.
facts.quote: Work began in autumn 1959 and the theatre was festively inaugurated on 15 April 1964.

facts.fact: In 2002–2003 it gained modern stage technology while the distinctive 1960s architecture was kept intact.
facts.quote: Hence, in 2002–2003 the building was equipped with modern facilities and technical features, satisfying European requirements in regard to stage technology and facility management while the distinctive architecture of the original 1960s building remained intact.

facts.fact: The renovation was entrusted to Kurt Gerling and Werner Arendt of Berlin.
facts.quote: The work was entrusted to Kurt Gerling and Werner Arendt of Gerling + Arendt Planungsgesellschaft mbH of Berlin.

facts.fact: It has two auditoriums: a 943-seat main theatre and a studio of up to 400 seats.
facts.quote: The theatre consists of two auditoriums: the main theatre with 943 seats and the studio which has up to 400 seats but can be compartmentalized.

facts.fact: It stands on the north-east corner of the Rond-Point Schumann, between the Glacis and the Red Bridge.
facts.quote: The Grand Théâtre is located on the north-eastern corner of the Rond-Point Schumann, between the Glacis, where there is plenty of parking space, and the Red Bridge.

facts.fact: It hosted the Eurovision Song Contest in 1973 and 1984.
facts.quote: The theatre has twice been the host venue for the Eurovision Song Contest, in 1973 and again in 1984.

facts.fact: Eye Filmmuseum is a film archive, museum and cinema in Amsterdam.
facts.quote: Eye Filmmuseum is a film archive, museum, and cinema in Amsterdam that preserves and presents both Dutch and foreign films screened in the Netherlands.

facts.fact: It stands in the Overhoeks neighbourhood of Amsterdam.
facts.quote: Eye Filmmuseum is located in the Overhoeks neighborhood of Amsterdam in the Netherlands.

facts.fact: In 2009 plans were announced for a new home on the north bank of Amsterdam's waterfront.
facts.quote: In 2009, Nederlands Filmmuseum merged with Holland Film, the Netherlands Institute for Film Education and the Filmbank and plans were announced for a new home on the north bank of Amsterdam's waterfront.

facts.fact: Queen Beatrix officially opened it on 4 April 2012.
facts.quote: The Filmmuseum was renamed the Eye Film Institute Netherlands and was officially opened on 4 April 2012, by Queen Beatrix.

facts.fact: The building was designed by Delugan Meissl Associated Architects, who also designed the Porsche Museum in Stuttgart.
facts.quote: The Eye Filmmuseum building is designed by Delugan Meissl Associated Architects, whose other projects include the Porsche Museum in Stuttgart.

facts.fact: It has two exhibition galleries, a 300-seat cinema, two 127-seat cinemas and a small cinema of about 67 seats.
facts.quote: The building features two gallery exhibition spaces, one 300-seat cinema, two 127-seat cinemas, and a fourth intimate cinema of about 67 seats.

facts.fact: Gustave Strauven designed the Saint-Cyr House, built 1901–1903 in Art Nouveau style.
facts.quote: It was designed by the architect Gustave Strauven, and built between 1901 and 1903, in Art Nouveau style.

facts.fact: It is Strauven's most important building, made as the home of painter and decorator George Léonard de Saint-Cyr.
facts.quote: It is Strauven's most important building, and served as a private residence for the painter and decorator George Léonard de Saint-Cyr.

facts.fact: Strauven had begun his career as an assistant designer to Victor Horta.
facts.quote: The Saint-Cyr House was designed and built by the architect Gustave Strauven, who began his career as an assistant designer working with Victor Horta.

facts.fact: Only 4 m (13 ft) wide, it was given great height through Strauven's inventions.
facts.quote: The Saint-Cyr House is only 4 metres (13 ft) wide, but was given extraordinary height through Strauven's elaborate architectural inventions.

facts.fact: The facade is covered in polychrome brick with abundant wrought iron and ornate balustrades on every floor.
facts.quote: The façade, marked by a flamboyant Art Nouveau style, is entirely covered by polychrome bricks and has a large amount of wrought iron, which is adorned with geometric motifs and ornate balustrades at each floor.

facts.fact: Its ironwork mimics plants and fills every space, so it has been called Art Nouveau-Baroque.
facts.quote: The wrought iron mimics vegetation and the decorative elements occupy all the space available. Due to its extravagance, the building has been called Art Nouveau-Baroque.

facts.fact: It was listed as a historic monument on 8 August 1988.
facts.quote: Always coveted by architecture enthusiasts, the building, listed as a historic monument on 8 August 1988, has had several owners.

facts.fact: Architect Francis Metzger (MA²) restored it by March 2013.
facts.quote: The house had been in a poor state of repair, but as of March 2013, has been restored to its former splendour by the architect Francis Metzger, from the architectural office MA² - Metzger et Associés Architecture.

facts.fact: Villa Empain is an Art Deco house in Brussels by Michel Polak for Baron Louis Empain, built 1930–1934.
facts.quote: It was designed by the Swiss-Belgian architect Michel Polak for Baron Louis Empain, the son of the industrialist Édouard Empain, and built between 1930 and 1934, in Art Deco style.

facts.fact: It has polished granite facades, marble and bronze, a courtyard and a swimming pool.

facts.fact: It is considered one of the finest Art Deco buildings in Brussels.

facts.fact: It drew wide interest in Belgium, where such Art Deco houses were rare, and used costly stone facings from around the world.

facts.fact: RTL used it from 1980 to 1993, and it stood empty after 1995.

facts.fact: Architect Francis Metzger (MA²) restored it in 2009–2010, and it reopened as a museum and cultural centre.
facts.quote: It was restored between 2009 and 2010 by the architect Francis Metzger, from the architectural office MA² - Metzger et Associés Architecture, and reopened to the public as a museum and cultural centre.

facts.fact: The conservation project won the EU Prize for Cultural Heritage / Europa Nostra Award in 2011.
facts.quote: The conservation project was awarded the European Union Prize for Cultural Heritage / Europa Nostra Award in 2011.

facts.fact: The Olympic Stadium was the main stadium of the 1928 Summer Olympics in Amsterdam.

facts.fact: Jan Wils designed it, and it is one of the finest examples of Amsterdam School architecture, matching Berlage's surrounding neighbourhood.
facts.quote: The Olympic Stadium was designed by architect Jan Wils, and is one of the finest examples of Amsterdamse School architecture, complementing the surrounding neighbourhood designed by H.P. Berlage.

facts.fact: The design won the Olympic gold medal in the 1928 architecture competition.

facts.fact: The Olympic flame burned for the first time in the Marathon tower beside the stadium.

facts.fact: After Rotterdam's De Kuip opened in 1937, a second ring raised capacity to 64,000.

facts.fact: The original 2014 design, with an elevated running track overlooking the pitch and city skyline views, was voted best design by Stadiumdb.com.
facts.quote: In 2014, the original designs of the new Puskás Ferenc stadium was voted the best design by Stadiumdb.com which complimented the imaginative design which included an elevated running track that overlooked the pitch and had city skyline views.

facts.fact: The arena opened on 15 November 2019 with a match between Hungary and Uruguay.
facts.quote: On 15 November 2019 the arena was opened by the match Hungary-Uruguay.

facts.fact: It hosted the 2026 UEFA Champions League final between Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal.
facts.quote: On 30 May 2026, Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal played in the 2026 UEFA Champions League final with PSG winning a 4–3 penalty shootout after a 1–1 draw.

facts.fact: The tower was built to improve telecommunications for the 1980 Moscow Olympics sailing regatta.
facts.quote: Tallinn TV Tower (Estonian: Tallinna teletorn) is a free-standing structure with an observation deck, built to provide better telecommunication services for the 1980 Moscow Summer Olympics regatta event (see Sailing at the 1980 Summer Olympics).

facts.fact: At 313 m it is the tallest non-building structure in Tallinn.
facts.quote: With its 313 m (1030.2 ft), the TV tower is the tallest nonbuilding structure in Tallinn.

facts.fact: The architects were David Baziladze and Juri Sinis, with engineers Vladimir Obydov and Yevgeny Ignatov.
facts.quote: The architects were David Baziladze and Juri Sinis, the engineers Vladimir Obydov and Yevgeny Ignatov.

facts.fact: The cornerstone was laid on 30 September 1975 and the tower was inaugurated on 11 July 1980.
facts.quote: The cornerstone was laid on 30 September 1975, and the building was inaugurated 11 July 1980 (although the first transmission took place in 1979).

facts.fact: Its body is made of reinforced concrete rings 50 cm thick, weighing 17,000 tonnes in total.
facts.quote: The tower body was constructed of reinforced concrete rings 50 cm thick that weigh a total of 17,000 tonnes, and the total tower weight is approximately 20,000 tonnes.

facts.fact: It is a 190 m reinforced concrete tower topped by a 124 m metal mast.
facts.quote: The structure consists of a 190-metre reinforced concrete tower and a 124-metre metal mast on top of it.

facts.fact: The observation deck on the 21st floor is 170 m above ground and 38 m across.
facts.quote: The observation deck on the 21st floor, originally designed to have a rotating section, is located 170 m above ground and has a diameter of 38 m.

facts.fact: The concrete tower was built using the sliding mould method.
facts.quote: The reinforced concrete tower itself was assembled using the sliding mold method.

facts.fact: It reopened on 5 April 2012 with a new interior designed by KOKO Arhitektid.
facts.quote: The Tallinn TV tower was reopened on 5 April 2012 with completely new interior design made by KOKO Arhitektid.

facts.fact: The Grand Hotel stands on Mother Theresa Boulevard in downtown Pristina, the capital of Kosovo.
facts.quote: The Grand Hotel Prishtina is a hotel situated in the Mother Theresa Boulevard in downtown Pristina, the capital of Kosovo.

facts.fact: It was designed by Albanian architect Bashkim Fehmiu with Serbian architects Dragan Kovačević and Miša Jevremović, and built from 1974 to 1978.
facts.quote: Originally projected by the Albanian architect Bashkim Fehmiu together with the two Serbian architects Dragan Kovačević and Miša Jevremović, its building started in 1974 and was completed in 1978.

facts.fact: The hotel has 350 rooms on 13 floors and covers over 32,000 m2.
facts.quote: The hotel features 350 rooms spread out on 13 floors, and covers a total area of over 32,000 m2 (340,000 sq ft).

facts.fact: The hotel came out of the socialist urban development of Pristina.
facts.quote: The concept of the Grand Hotel in Prishtina came alongside the socialist urban development of the city.

facts.fact: Bashkim Fehmiu was the first Albanian architect educated at the University of Belgrade's Faculty of Architecture.
facts.quote: Thus, the design was handed over to Bashkim Fehmiu, the first Albanian architect educated in Belgrade in the University of Belgrade, Faculty of Architecture.

facts.fact: The interior was curated by Kosovar artist Matej Rodiqi.
facts.quote: The interior of the hotel was curated by the Kosovar artist Matej Rodiqi.

facts.fact: During the Manifesta 14 biennale, floors 3 to 9 held exhibitions by more than 30 artists.
facts.quote: The hotel's 3rd to 9th floors hosted exhibitions by over 30 artists from Kosovo as well as from the international art scene.

facts.fact: Zetra Olympic Hall, renamed after Juan Antonio Samaranch, is an indoor multi-purpose arena in Sarajevo.
facts.quote: The Juan Antonio Samaranch Olympic Hall, also known as Zetra Olympic Hall, is an indoor multi-purpose arena in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

facts.fact: Construction began in June 1981 and the hall was opened on 14 February 1982.
facts.quote: The construction of the complex started in June 1981 and was officially opened by then-President of the International Olympic Committee, Juan Antonio Samaranch, on 14 February 1982.

facts.fact: It was built specifically for the 1984 Winter Olympics in Sarajevo.
facts.quote: Zetra Olympic Hall was constructed specifically for the 1984 Winter Olympics, hosted in Sarajevo, and was completed in 1982.

facts.fact: It was described as an ultramodern, angular building with a copper roof.
facts.quote: It was described as an "ultramodern, angular edifice" with a copper roof.

facts.fact: The hall was badly damaged by shelling, bombing and fire on 25 May 1992 during the Bosnian War.
facts.quote: The arena suffered substantial damage from shelling, bombing and fire by the Serb forces on Monday, May 25, 1992 during the Bosnian War.

facts.fact: During the war its wooden seats were used to make coffins for civilians killed in the fighting.
facts.quote: The wooden seats from the venue were used as material for coffins for civilians killed in the war.

facts.fact: Reconstruction began in September 1997 without the original blueprints, which were never recovered.
facts.quote: Although the original blueprints were never recovered, in September 1997, reconstruction on the venue, facilitated by the SFOR, began.

facts.fact: The reconstruction was completed in 1999.
facts.quote: The reconstruction was completed in 1999.

facts.fact: The bridge crosses the Neretva and links the two parts of Mostar, a city named after the bridge keepers who guarded it in Ottoman times.
facts.quote: It crosses the river Neretva and connects the two parts of the city, which is named after the bridge keepers (mostari) who guarded the Old Bridge during the Ottoman era.

facts.fact: It was commissioned by Suleiman the Magnificent in 1557 and designed by Mimar Hayruddin, a student of Mimar Sinan.
facts.quote: Commissioned by Suleiman the Magnificent in 1557 and designed by Mimar Hayruddin, a student and apprentice of the architect Mimar Sinan, the Old Bridge is an exemplary piece of Balkan Islamic architecture.

facts.fact: The hump-backed bridge is 4 m wide and 30 m long and stands 24 m above the river.
facts.quote: The Stari Most is hump-backed, 4 metres (13 ft 1 in) wide and 30 metres (98 ft 5 in) long, and dominates the river from a height of 24 m (78 ft 9 in).

facts.fact: Instead of foundations, it rests on limestone abutments tied to wing walls along the cliffs.
facts.quote: Instead of foundations, the bridge has abutments of limestone linked to wing walls along the waterside cliffs.

facts.fact: It replaced a wooden suspension bridge hung on chains.
facts.quote: The old bridge on the river "...was made of wood and hung on chains," wrote the Ottoman geographer Katip Çelebi, and it "...swayed so much that people crossing it did so in mortal fear".

facts.fact: When it was completed it was the widest human-made arch in the world.
facts.quote: Upon its completion, it was the widest human-made arch in the world.

facts.fact: The bridge collapsed on 9 November 1993 after shelling by Bosnian Croat forces.
facts.quote: Slobodan Praljak, the commander of the Croat Defence Council, ordered the destruction of the bridge, which collapsed on 9 November 1993 as a result of shelling by the Bosnian Croat forces.

facts.fact: It was rebuilt as closely as possible to the original, using the same technology and materials.
facts.quote: It was decided to build a bridge as similar as possible to the original, using the same technology and materials.

facts.fact: Reconstruction began on 7 June 2001 and the bridge was inaugurated on 23 July 2004.
facts.quote: Reconstruction commenced on 7 June 2001. The reconstructed bridge was inaugurated on 23 July 2004, with the cost estimated to be 15.5 million US dollars.

facts.fact: The memorial marks the Battle of Kadinjača on 29 November 1941 and the end of the Republic of Užice, and was declared a Monument of Culture of Exceptional Importance in 1979.
facts.quote: Kadinjača Memorial, which memorializes the 29 November 1941 Battle on Kadinjača during the World War II and the end of the Ужичка Република, Užička Republika, or the Republic of Užice, was declared Monument of Culture of Exceptional Importance in 1979, and it is protected by Republic of Serbia.

facts.fact: The complex is made of parts built between 1952 and 1979.
facts.quote: The memorial is of a complex architectural museal form, comprising the segments built between the years 1952 and 1979.

facts.fact: The first part, from 1952, is a pyramid-shaped obelisk over a crypt holding the remains of the Workers' Battalion fighters.
facts.quote: In the first phase (in 1952), the Kadinjača monument was erected under the pyramidal obelisk shape which is the crypt where the remains of members of the Workers' battalion killed during the Battle of Kadinjača lie.

facts.fact: A 1979 expansion by sculptor Miodrag Živković and architect Aleksandar Đokić gave the complex its present form.
facts.quote: A significant complex expansion took place in 1979, when - based on a project by sculptor Miodrag Živković and architect Aleksandar Đokić - it received its present appearance.

facts.fact: The complex was opened by Yugoslav President Josip Broz Tito on 23 September 1979.
facts.quote: The entire memorial complex was officially opened by the President of the SFRJ, Josip Broz Tito, on 23 September 1979.

facts.fact: Its exhibition holds over three hundred items and documents, mostly about members of the Workers' Battalion.
facts.quote: A special segment of the exhibition complex are over three hundred items and authentic documents, mostly related to members of the Workers Battalion.

facts.fact: Živković was a Serbian sculptor known for memorial complexes across Yugoslavia.
facts.quote: He is well-known for his work on memorial complexes throughout Yugoslavia.

facts.fact: Seimas Palace is the seat of the Seimas, Lithuania's parliament, in Vilnius.
facts.quote: Seimas Palace (Lithuanian: Seimo rūmai) is the seat of the Seimas, the Lithuanian parliament.

facts.fact: The decision to build a seat for the Supreme Soviet of the Lithuanian SSR was made in 1969, on the site of a youth football stadium on Gediminas Avenue.
facts.quote: The decision to build a seat for the Supreme Soviet of Lithuanian SSR was made in 1969. The location of the Youth Football Stadium, in the Gediminas Avenue, was chosen for the project.

facts.fact: Architects Algimantas and Vytautas Nasvytis designed it and chose a square plan for the main building.
facts.quote: Architects Algimantas Nasvytis and Vytautas Nasvytis were chosen to design and supervise the project and decided on a square plan for the main building of the complex.

facts.fact: Construction of the first wing began in 1976, and 9,717 m2 of the palace were completed in 1980.
facts.quote: In 1976, the construction works began on the first wing of the palace. In 1980, 9717.37 square meters of the palace were completed.

facts.fact: The finished complex has three wings; the first holds the Parliament Hall.
facts.quote: The final phase of the palace complex consists of three wings, with the main, or first wing, housing the Parliament Hall, where legislation is passed.

facts.fact: Lithuania's independence was re-established in the old Parliament Hall on 11 March 1990.
facts.quote: On 11 March 1990, Lithuania's independence was re-established in the old Parliament Hall, where the re-establishment declaration from the Soviet Union was adopted.

facts.fact: A new Parliament Hall opened on 10 September 2007.
facts.quote: On 10 September 2007, the new Parliament Hall was officially opened.

facts.fact: The twin brothers Algimantas and Vytautas Nasvytis often worked together.
facts.quote: Nasvytis often cooperated with his twin brother Vytautas Nasvytis.

facts.fact: The monument is a World War II memorial sculpture by Dušan Džamonja in Podgarić, Croatia.
facts.quote: Monument to the Revolution of the people of Moslavina  or simply Monument to the Revolution (Croatian: Spomenik revoluciji naroda Moslavine or Spomenik revoluciji) is a World War II memorial sculpture by Dušan Džamonja, located in Podgarić, Berek municipality, Croatia.

facts.fact: It stands about 10 m high and 20 m long.
facts.quote: The monument stands about 10 m high and is 20 m long.

facts.fact: It is dedicated to the people of Moslavina in World War II.
facts.quote: It is dedicated to the people of Moslavina during World War II.

facts.fact: It was inspired by Nike, the Greek goddess of victory, and set into the landscape.
facts.quote: The monument is inspired by the Greek mythological goddess of victory Nike. Džamonja built it immersed in the landscape.

facts.fact: The central metal structure is a stylised sun with two asymmetric wings.
facts.quote: The metallic structure in the center represents a stylized sun, which is given two asymmetric wings on the sides.

facts.fact: It was dedicated in 1967 by Yugoslav President Josip Broz Tito.
facts.quote: The monument was dedicated in 1967 by the president of Yugoslavia, Josip Broz Tito.

facts.fact: The monument, known locally as the Russian Monument, is a large concrete memorial complex on Turna Tepe hill in northern Varna.
facts.quote: Park-Monument of the Bulgarian-Soviet Friendship (Bulgarian: Парк-паметник на българо-съветската дружба), also known locally as the Russian Monument, is a large concrete memorial complex on Turna Tepe hill in the northern part of Varna, Bulgaria.

facts.fact: At 23 m high and 48 m wide, it is the largest monument in the Varna region.
facts.quote: At 23 metres high and 48 metres wide, it is the largest monument in the Varna region, and it remains one of the more prominent surviving examples of large-scale socialist-era memorial architecture in Bulgaria, alongside sites such as Buzludzha and the Founders of the Bulgarian State monument in Shumen.

facts.fact: The design came from a 1973 competition won by architect Kamen Goranov with sculptors Evgeni Barumov and Alyosha Kafedzhiyski; ground was broken on 4 November 1974.
facts.quote: A design competition was held in the autumn of 1973, and the winning proposal, submitted by architect Kamen Goranov together with sculptors Evgeni Barumov (also transliterated Barmov) and Alyosha Kafedzhiyski, was approved for construction. Ground was broken on 4 November 1974.

facts.fact: More than 10,000 tonnes of concrete and about 1,000 tonnes of reinforcing steel were used.
facts.quote: More than 10,000 tonnes of concrete and around 1,000 tonnes of reinforcing steel were used to build the structure and the roughly 400-square-metre platform on which it stands.

facts.fact: The two wing-like concrete forms open out from a central axis, often likened to a bird in flight facing the Black Sea.
facts.quote: The monument takes the form of two large, wing-like concrete forms that open outward from a central axis, an arrangement often described as evoking a bird in flight looking out toward the Black Sea and, symbolically, toward the Soviet Union beyond it.

facts.fact: A staircase of 301 steps, the 'Staircase of Victory', leads up the hill to the monument.
facts.quote: The surrounding hillside was landscaped as a park, with tens of thousands of trees and shrubs planted, and a monumental staircase of 301 steps—known as the "Staircase of Victory"—was built leading from the base of the hill to the summit; including the connecting park alleys, the total number of steps on the site is said to exceed 2,400.

facts.fact: It was formally inaugurated on 13 November 1978.
facts.quote: The completed park-monument was formally inaugurated on 13 November 1978, in a ceremony that reportedly included a tourist information point, a small bookshop and gift shop, and an eternal flame set into a bronze cube in front of the main structure.

facts.fact: Since 1989 it has not been maintained by the state and has fallen into disrepair.
facts.quote: Since the political changes of 1989, the monument has not been maintained by the state and has fallen into disrepair; its bronze inscriptions have largely been stripped by metal thieves and its interior spaces have been sealed off to visitors since around 2019.

facts.fact: The Telephone Palace is an Art Deco office building on Calea Victoriei in Bucharest.
facts.quote: Telephones Company Building (Romanian: Palatul Telefoanelor) is an Art Deco office building located on Calea Victoriei in Bucharest, Romania.

facts.fact: Until 1956 it was the tallest building in Bucharest, at 52.5 m.
facts.quote: Palatul Telefoanelor in Bucharest is an Art Deco style building and until 1956, was the tallest building in Bucharest at 52.5 metres (172 feet).

facts.fact: It was built for the Romanian Telephone Company (SART), formed by ITT after it won a monopoly on Romanian telephony.
facts.quote: The Romanian government decided to take a loan from the American trust, J.P. Morgan & Co.,  which obtained from this transaction the granting of a 20-year monopoly on Romanian telephony to the International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation (ITT), which then formed the Societatea Anonimă Română de Telefoane (SART, "Romanian Telephone Company, Ltd."). The aim was to modernize Romanian telephony and to construct the Telephone Palace.

facts.fact: Designed by Edmond Van Saanen Algi and built in about 20 months in 1931–1933, it was the first major modernist building on Calea Victoriei.
facts.quote: Designed on behalf of SART by the Romanian architect of Dutch origin Edmond Van Saanen Algi and built over the course of about 20 months in 1931–1933, it was the first major modernist building on Bucharest's Calea Victoriei, the street of which Tudor Octavian wrote, "this is how the whole of Bucharest would look if we had been allowed..., if its builders had been clever enough..."

facts.fact: Its steel skeleton came from the Reșița steelworks, and it was inaugurated in 1934 in the presence of King Carol II.
facts.quote: The steel skeleton was produced by the Reșița steelworks. The building was inaugurated in 1934 in the presence of King Carol II.

facts.fact: It was extended in 1940 and 1946 and survived several earthquakes and wartime bombing in 1944.
facts.quote: The building was extended (both vertically and horizontally) in 1940 and 1946, and survived earthquakes in 1940, 1977, 1986, and 1990, as well as bombing in 1944 by Allied Forces during World War II.

facts.fact: A reconstruction, designed by Proiect Bucuresti, copied the original façade and strengthened the structure.
facts.quote: Work included reconstruction to duplicate the original façade, as well as structural reinforcement. The reconstruction design was made by Romanian architecture office Proiect Bucuresti.

facts.fact: The building served as the Administrative and Justice Palace until 1955, when it was given to four museums, now the Moldavia National Museum Complex.
facts.quote: The building served as the Administrative and Justice Palace until 1955, when its designation and use was changed, and assigned to the four museums nowadays united under the name of Moldavia National Museum Complex.

facts.fact: It is listed in Romania's National Register of Historic Monuments.
facts.quote: The Palace of Culture is listed in the National Register of Historic Monuments.

facts.fact: It stands within the medieval Princely Court of Moldavia and rebuilt the former Princely Palace, keeping its foundations and first two floors.
facts.quote: Located in the perimeter of the medieval Princely Court of Moldavia (from 1434), the construction was conceived as a rebuilding and expansion project of the former Princely Palace of Moldavia, dated to the time of Prince Alexandru Moruzi (1803–1806, architect Johann Freywald), and renovated by Prince Mihail Sturdza (1841–1843, architect Nicolai Sungurov), from which it preserved the foundations and first two floors.

facts.fact: Architect I. D. Berindei designed it in a flamboyant Neo-Gothic style, unlike the neoclassical old palace.
facts.quote: Unlike the old palace, built in a neoclassical style, Berindei chose to design it in a flamboyant Neo-Gothic style.

facts.fact: Work started in 1906–1907, stopped during World War I, and was completed on 11 October 1925.
facts.quote: Started in 1906–1907, the reconstruction works were halted during World War I, due to the limitation of resources, but the unfinished building sheltered Romanian and Russian troops, and different public institutions and military hospitals. The monument was finally completed on 11 October 1925, and officially inaugurated one year later, by King Ferdinand I of Romania.

facts.fact: The palace has 298 large rooms with a total area of 34,236 m2.
facts.quote: The Palace has 298 large rooms with a total area of 34,236 m2 (368,510 sq ft), 92 windows in the front part of the building and another 36 inside the building.

facts.fact: Despite its archaic look, it was designed with modern materials and technology, replacing stone blocks with lighter, cheaper materials.
facts.quote: In spite of its archaic-looking design, the Palace was designed so to integrate modern materials and technologies. Thus, the stone blocks were replaced with light and much cheaper materials.

facts.fact: The entrance is through a great crenellated tower, the central architectural piece of the palace.
facts.quote: The entrance of the palace is through a great donjon tower, with crenels and alcoves dominated by an eagle with open wings. The tower is the central architectural piece of the palace.

facts.fact: A major restoration began in 2008, with the main works finished in April 2016.
facts.quote: A large-scale restoration project, considered one of the most complex in Romania since 1990, began in 2008. The main works were completed in April 2016.

facts.fact: The bridge crosses the Drina River in Višegrad, Bosnia and Herzegovina.
facts.quote: The Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge (Serbian: Мост Мехмед-паше Соколовића, romanized: Most Mehmed-paše Sokolovića) is a historic bridge over the Drina River in Višegrad, in the Republika Srpska region of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

facts.fact: It was completed in 1577 by Ottoman court architect Mimar Sinan for Grand Vizier Mehmed Paša Sokolović.
facts.quote: It was completed in 1577 by the Ottoman court architect Mimar Sinan on the order of the Grand Vizier Mehmed Paša Sokolović.

facts.fact: It became a national monument of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 2003 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.
facts.quote: In 2003 bridge was included into the List of National Monuments of Bosnia and Herzegovina by KONS, and UNESCO inclusion into the World Heritage List followed in 2007.

facts.fact: It has 11 masonry arches spanning 11 to 15 m, and a right-angled ramp on the west bank.
facts.quote: It comprises 11 masonry arches, with spans of 11 to 15 meters, and a right-angled approach ramp on the west bank of the river.

facts.fact: The bridge is 179.5 m long.
facts.quote: The 179.5-meter-long (589 ft) bridge was designed by Mimar Sinan, one of the greatest architects and engineers of the classical Ottoman period and a contemporary of the Italian Renaissance.

facts.fact: The Grand Vizier commissioned it as a tribute to his native region and a symbol of trade and prosperity; it was built between 1571 and 1577.
facts.quote: The Višegrad Bridge was commissioned by Grand Vizier Mehmed Pasha Sokolović, who exercised power over a long period at the summit of the Ottoman Empire during the reigns of three sultans, as a tribute to his native region and a symbol of trade and prosperity. Construction of the bridge took place between 1571 and 1577.

facts.fact: Three arches were destroyed in World War I and five damaged in World War II, all later restored.
facts.quote: Three of its 11 arches were destroyed during World War I and five were damaged during World War II but subsequently restored.

facts.fact: The bridge is widely known from Ivo Andrić's 1945 novel The Bridge on the Drina.
facts.quote: The bridge is widely known because of the 1945 book The Bridge on the Drina, by Nobel Prize–winning Yugoslav writer Ivo Andrić.

facts.fact: Peleș is a Neo-Renaissance palace in the Carpathian Mountains near Sinaia, built between 1873 and 1914 for King Carol I and inaugurated in 1883.
facts.quote: Peleș Castle (Romanian: Castelul Peleș pronounced [kaˈstelul ˈpeleʃ] ) is a Neo-Renaissance palace in the Royal Domain of Sinaia in the Carpathian Mountains, near Sinaia, in Prahova County, Romania, on an existing medieval route linking Transylvania and Wallachia, built between 1873 and 1914. Its inauguration was held in 1883.

facts.fact: It was built as a royal hunting preserve and summer retreat; the foundation was laid on 22 August 1873.
facts.quote: The King commissioned the construction of a royal hunting preserve and summer retreat on the property, and the foundation was laid for Peleș Castle on 22 August 1873.

facts.fact: It was the world's first castle fully powered by electricity produced on site.
facts.quote: Peleș became the world's first castle fully powered by locally produced electricity.

facts.fact: The king rejected three earlier plans that copied Western European palaces as unoriginal and too costly.
facts.quote: The first three design plans submitted for Peleș were copies of other palaces in Western Europe, and King Carol I rejected them all as lacking originality and being too costly.

facts.fact: German architect Johannes Schultz won with a palatial alpine castle mixing Italian elegance and German aesthetics along Renaissance lines.
facts.quote: German architect Johannes Schultz won the project by presenting a more original plan, something that appealed to the King's taste: a grand palatial alpine castle combining different features of classic European styles, mostly following Italian elegance and German aesthetics along Renaissance lines.

facts.fact: Czech architect Karel Liman added the towers between 1893 and 1914, including the 66 m main tower.
facts.quote: Later additions were made between 1893 and 1914 by the Czech architect Karel Liman, who designed the towers, including the main central tower, which is 66 metres (217 ft) in height.

facts.fact: Its style blends Neo-Renaissance and Gothic Revival, similar to Neuschwanstein Castle in Bavaria.
facts.quote: Its architectural style is a romantically inspired blend Neo-Renaissance and Gothic Revival similar to Neuschwanstein Castle in Bavaria.

facts.fact: The courtyard façades show Saxon influence, with painted murals and ornate half-timbering.
facts.quote: A Saxon influence can be observed in the interior courtyard facades, which have allegorical hand-painted murals and ornate fachwerk similar to that seen in northern European alpine architecture.

facts.fact: The opera house on Andrássy Avenue was designed by Miklós Ybl, a major figure of 19th-century Hungarian architecture.
facts.quote: Originally known as the Hungarian Royal Opera House, it was designed by Miklós Ybl, a major figure of 19th-century Hungarian architecture.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1875, funded by the city and by Emperor Franz Joseph I, and it opened on 27 September 1884.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1875, funded by the city of Budapest and by Emperor Franz Joseph I of Austria-Hungary, and the new house opened to the public on the 27 September 1884.

facts.fact: It was built in neo-Renaissance style with Baroque elements.
facts.quote: It was built in neo-Renaissance style, with elements of Baroque.

facts.fact: The horseshoe-shaped auditorium seats 1,261 and was measured in the 1970s as having the third best acoustics in Europe, after La Scala and the Palais Garnier.
facts.quote: The auditorium holds 1,261 people. It is horseshoe-shaped and – according to measurements done in the 1970s by a group of international engineers – has the third best acoustics in Europe after La Scala in Milan and the Palais Garnier in Paris.

facts.fact: The decoration of the symmetrical façade follows a musical theme.
facts.quote: The decoration of the symmetrical façade follows a musical theme.

facts.fact: The main hall has a 3,050 kg bronze chandelier lighting a fresco by Károly Lotz of the Greek gods on Olympus.
facts.quote: The main hall is decorated with a bronze chandelier weighing 3050 kg. It illuminates a fresco by Károly Lotz, depicting the Greek gods on Olympus.

facts.fact: The stage used the most modern technology of its time, with a revolving stage and hydraulic machinery.
facts.quote: The central stage proscenium arch employed the most modern technology of the time. It featured a revolving stage and metal hydraulic machinery.

facts.fact: A restoration that returned the house to its original look and added new stage machinery ended with its reopening on 12 March 2022.
facts.quote: It returned the house to its original appearance and added modern technology, including new stage machinery, and the Opera House reopened on 12 March 2022 with a three-day festival.

facts.fact: The hotel was completed in 1956 in the socialist realism style and is a Czech cultural monument.
facts.quote: It was completed in 1956 in the socialist realism style, and is a Czech cultural monument.

facts.fact: It was originally designed as a military hotel and has kept much of its original interior artwork.
facts.quote: The hotel has retained much of its original interior artwork, contains 278 guest rooms, and was originally designed as a military hotel before public use as a luxury hotel.

facts.fact: It was built from 1952 to 1956, with interior decoration finished in 1957.
facts.quote: Construction of the hotel took place from 1952 to 1956, with interior decorations finished in 1957.

facts.fact: Architect František Jeřábek worked with the military on new plans that included a luxury hotel.
facts.quote: The final construction site for the new hotel was chosen in 1951, and architect František Jeřábek worked with the military on a new set of plans, which were more complicated and included a luxury hotel.

facts.fact: At 88 m it is the largest Stalinist building in Prague, inspired by Moscow's Seven Sisters.
facts.quote: It is the largest Stalinist architecture building in Prague at 88 meters (289 ft) tall, and was inspired by the Seven Sisters in Moscow.

facts.fact: It has two symmetrical wings around a large central tower.
facts.quote: The hotel is divided into two symmetrical wings, with a large central tower, and the former officers' gym was converted into a convention hall with a bar.

facts.fact: The entrance hall and main staircase have stucco and painted ceilings, marble columns and wall artworks meant to feel palatial.
facts.quote: The entrance hall and the main staircase include a stucco and painted ceiling, marble columns, and artworks on its walls to create a palatial atmosphere.

facts.fact: The largest tapestry, Praga Regina Musicae, hangs in the entrance hall.
facts.quote: The largest tapestry called Praga Regina Musicae is located in the entrance hall, and features a view of Prague with the former Stalin monument in Letná Park in the middle.

facts.fact: Praha hlavní nádraží is Prague's largest railway station; it opened in 1871 as Franz Josef Station.
facts.quote: Praha hlavní nádraží (IATA: XYG) is the largest railway station in Prague, Czech Republic. It opened in 1871 as Franz Josef Station, after Franz Joseph I of Austria.

facts.fact: It is the largest Art Nouveau monument in the Czech Republic and a cultural monument since 1976.
facts.quote: The station is the largest Art Nouveau monument in the Czech Republic. Since 31 December 1976, it has been a cultural monument of the Czech Republic and since 1993 it has been part of the urban monument zone of Vinohrady, Žižkov and Vršovice.

facts.fact: The Art Nouveau station building and hall were built in 1901–1909 to designs by Czech architect Josef Fanta, replacing the old Neo-Renaissance station.
facts.quote: The Art Nouveau station building and station hall were built between 1901 and 1909, designed by Czech architect Josef Fanta on the site of the old dismantled Neo-Renaissance station designed by Czech architects Antonín Viktor Barvitius and Vojtěch Ignác Ullmann.

facts.fact: The dome is decorated with Art Nouveau motifs and sculptures by Stanislav Sucharda and Ladislav Šaloun depicting Czech cities.
facts.quote: The dome above the main part of the building is decorated with art nouveau motifs and sculptures by Stanislav Sucharda and Ladislav Šaloun depicting Czech cities.

facts.fact: The tracks were roofed in 1905–1906 by a two-nave steel arched hall, 2 × 33.3 m wide, 18 m high and 233 m long, by Jaroslav Marjanko and Rudolf Kornfeld.
facts.quote: Underpasses were built together with the new building, the railway yard was roofed in 1905–1906 by a two-nave steel arched hall with a span of 2 x 33.3 m, a height of 18 m and a length of 233 m, the authors of which were Jaroslav Marjanko and Rudolf Kornfeld.

facts.fact: The original 150 m station building, with two towers, was nicknamed the 'castle station'.
facts.quote: The 150-metre-long building with two towers, a hall with a coffered ceiling, a restaurant, offices and 22 doors leading to a mosaic-paved platform has earned the nickname "castle station".

facts.fact: The station is connected to Prague Metro Line C.
facts.quote: The station is connected to Prague Metro Line C and the Hlavní nádraží railway station.

facts.fact: The mosque in Shah Alam is Malaysia's largest and the second largest in Southeast Asia by capacity.
facts.quote: It is located in Shah Alam and is the country's largest mosque and also the second largest mosque in Southeast Asia by capacity.

facts.fact: Its large blue and silver dome is its most distinctive feature, with a minaret at each of its four corners.
facts.quote: Its most distinguishing feature is its large blue and silver dome. The mosque has four minarets, one erected at each of the corners.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1982 and finished on 11 March 1988.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1982 and finished on 11 March 1988.

facts.fact: The dome is 51.2 m across and rises 106.7 m above the ground.
facts.quote: The mosque has the distinction of having one of the largest religious dome in the world, measuring 51.2 m (168 ft) in diameter and reaching 106.7 m (350 ft) above ground level.

facts.fact: The design combines Malay and Modernist styles.
facts.quote: The design of the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Mosque is a combination of Malay and Modernist styles, and elements of Malay and Islamic architecture are incorporated into the finishes of the building.

facts.fact: Blue stained-glass windows cut the light entering the hall, giving the interior a bluish glow.
facts.quote: The windows are fitted with blue stained glass to reduce the amount of light entering the hall. The resulting filtered illumination lends a bluish ambiance to the interior spaces, evoking a sense of peace and serenity.

facts.fact: The dome is built of aluminium, clad outside in enamelled triangular steel panels.
facts.quote: The dome is constructed of aluminium and the outer surface is clad with vitreous enamel-baked triangular steel panels decorated with a rosette of verses from the Qur'an.

facts.fact: The mosque holds 12,600 worshippers.
facts.quote: The mosque has the capacity to accommodate 12,600 worshippers and is large enough that on a clear day it can be seen from some vantage points in Kuala Lumpur.

facts.fact: The Palace of Justice is the courthouse complex for Malaysia's Federal Court and Court of Appeal, the country's two highest courts.
facts.quote: The Palace of Justice (Malay: Istana Kehakiman, Jawi: ايستان کحاکيمن) is a courthouse complex in Putrajaya that serves as the seat for Malaysia's Federal Court and Court of Appeal, which are the highest court and second highest court in the country, respectively.

facts.fact: The courts moved there from the Sultan Abdul Samad Building in Kuala Lumpur when it was completed in 2003.
facts.quote: The two courts were previously housed in the Sultan Abdul Samad Building in Kuala Lumpur, before being moved to their present location in 2003, when the construction of the Palace of Justice was completed.

facts.fact: The firm aQidea Architects designed it after finishing the nearby Prime Minister's Office.
facts.quote: The courthouse complex was built at Precinct 3 of Putrajaya, and aQidea Architects was the architectural firm commissioned to design the building after finishing the nearby Prime Minister's Office.

facts.fact: A network of passages keeps judges, witnesses, the public and the accused apart on their way to the courts.
facts.quote: The complex has an intricate network of passages that segregate the judges, witnesses, public, and the accused, leading to the courts from the car park or area of arrival.

facts.fact: Principal architect Ahmad Rozi Abd Wahab was responsible for the layout and the architectural concept, built around the theme of order.
facts.quote: The design is about bringing about "order", and order is the theme of the day as the layouts are fashioned in an orderly manner. AR Ahmad Rozi Abd Wahab, the principal architect, was personally responsible for the design layout and coming up with the architectural concept and ideas.

facts.fact: The design draws on Classical Islamic, Moorish and Western Classical (Palladian) influences.
facts.quote: The Palace of Justice's design incorporates influences of Classical Islamic culture like Taj Mahal in India, Moorish culture, like the Sultan Abdul Samad Building in Kuala Lumpur, and Western Classical influence, like Palladian.

facts.fact: The rooms are arranged around a large central rotunda that guides visitors through the building.
facts.quote: There is a large central atrium (Rotunda) around which the various rooms are arranged. The atrium helps to guide visitors who had just arrived into the building and has clear visual connection to the other floors above.

facts.fact: The five-storey building cost RM362 million on a 3.3-hectare site.
facts.quote: The 5-storey building, which cost RM362 million and was built at a 3.3 hectare site, will also house several holding cells and a police station.

facts.fact: The stadium in Kuala Lumpur is where Malaya's independence was formally declared on 31 August 1957.
facts.quote: It is known as the site of the formal declaration of independence of the Federation of Malaya on 31 August 1957.

facts.fact: It was designed by American architect Stanley Jewkes, under the instruction of Prime Minister Tunku Abdul Rahman.
facts.quote: The stadium was designed by American architect Stanley Jewkes, under the instruction of the first Prime Minister of Malaysia, Tunku Abdul Rahman.

facts.fact: It was built from 25 September 1956 to 21 August 1957.
facts.quote: The stadium was constructed from 25 September 1956 to 21 August 1957, and was designed by the then Director of Public Works Department, Stanley Edward Jewkes.

facts.fact: It was built as an earthed amphitheatre, partly below ground level.
facts.quote: The stadium was constructed as an earthed amphitheatre, which means that a part of the stadium is below ground level.

facts.fact: On completion it held world records for the tallest prestressed floodlight towers, at 120 feet, and the biggest cantilever shell roofs.
facts.quote: The stadium held two world records upon its completion: the tallest prestressed floodlight towers at 120 feet and the biggest cantilever shell roofs.

facts.fact: The concrete shell roof over the grandstand was chosen because it was both affordable and beautiful.
facts.quote: The shell roof for the grandstand, made out of concrete, was chosen as it was both economically affordable and aesthetically beautiful.

facts.fact: To save money, most materials were made locally and imported structural steel was avoided.
facts.quote: Due to budget constraints, most of the construction materials were made locally, which meant that imported materials such as structural steels had to be avoided.

facts.fact: It is a national heritage building and won a UNESCO Asia-Pacific Award for Heritage Conservation in 2008.
facts.quote: The stadium is currently a national heritage building. In 2008, the Independence Stadium received the UNESCO Asia-Pacific Award for Excellence for Heritage Conservation owing to its cultural significance and embodiment of a unique independence declaration event.

facts.fact: Sala Chalermkrung was built as a Modernist cinema on Charoengkrung Road in Bangkok and now hosts classical Thai dance.
facts.quote: Sala Chalermkrung Royal Theatre (Thai: ศาลาเฉลิมกรุง; RTGS: Sala Chaloem Krung) was originally a movie theatre in Bangkok, Thailand built in Modernist style on Charoengkrung Road. It was opened on 3 July 1933. After serving as a cinema for many years it now hosts performances of classical Thai dance.

facts.fact: King Prajadhipok sponsored it to mark Bangkok's 150th anniversary in 1932; its name means 'Pavilion to Celebrate the City'.
facts.quote: Construction of Sala Chalermkrung theatre was sponsored by King Prajadhipok as part of the celebrations in 1932 to mark the 150th anniversary of the founding of Bangkok. The name Sala Chalermkrung derives from this, meaning 'Pavilion to Celebrate the City'.

facts.fact: The architect was Mom Chao Samaichaloem Kridakorn, a recent Beaux-Arts graduate, at a time when such roles had always gone to Europeans.
facts.quote: The King chose as the architect for the project Mom Chao Samaichaloem Kridakorn who was at that time Chief Master Builder at the Department of Outer Palace. This was a bold choice since Kridakorn had only recently graduated in Beaux-Arts Architecture and such important roles had previously always been filled by Europeans.

facts.fact: The neon lights on top of the front façade, spelling the name in Thai, were the largest in Asia.
facts.quote: The neon lights on the top of the front facade displaying in Thai the name Sala Chalerm Krung were the largest in Asia.

facts.fact: It had modern air-conditioning, new to many Siamese at the time.
facts.quote: Plus the theatre was equipped with modern air-conditioning, a new experience for many Siamese at the time.

facts.fact: The main auditorium seated 1,500, with a second 350-seat auditorium and private rooms for royal screenings.
facts.quote: The main auditorium seated 1,500 patrons whilst there was a smaller 350 seat auditorium plus private rooms for royal screenings as well as dance rooms and a dining salon.

facts.fact: It was renovated in 1992 for traditional theatre, with a wider stage and a hydraulic stage lift, reducing seating to 600.
facts.quote: With the intended emphasis on traditional theatre rather than movies, the stage was widened and a hydraulic stage lift system installed. This has reduced seating to 600.

facts.fact: It stands in downtown Ho Chi Minh City's Saigon ward, with its front facing Nguyễn Huệ Boulevard.
facts.quote: It is located in downtown Ho Chi Minh City's Saigon ward,  between Pasteur, Lý Tự Trọng, Đồng Khởi, and Lê Thánh Tôn Street, with its front facade facing Nguyễn Huệ Boulevard.

facts.fact: It is one of Vietnam's national heritage sites.
facts.quote: The building now also serves as one of Vietnam's national heritage sites and is open for public at the last weekend of each month.

facts.fact: Ground was broken in 1898 after a canal was covered over, and the building took 11 years to finish.
facts.quote: Until 1898, after the canal was covered to be made into Charner Boulevard, the French finally broke ground for the building. 1.5 million francs was approved for the project. The building was a difficult project that took 11 years to finish.

facts.fact: It opened in 1909 to mark 50 years of French presence in Saigon.
facts.quote: The building was opened in 1909 by the French Indochina governors-general to celebrate 50 years of French presence in Saigon.

facts.fact: Designed under architect Fernand Gardès, it took its inspiration from the town hall of Paris and the bell towers of northern France.
facts.quote: Directed by architect Fernand Gardè, the hall design took inspiration from the town hall of Paris and resembles the bell towers of northern France – a rising point-shaped tower accompanied by two adequate symmetrical attic towers and shorter but long blocks on the sides.

facts.fact: Its design fuses Renaissance, Baroque and Beaux-Arts, with Art Nouveau iron doors and Corinthian columns.
facts.quote: The design of the building is a fusion of multiple classical architectural streams like Renaissance, Baroque and Beaux-Arts, as seen on its with Baroque and Rococo decoration, Art Nouveau iron doors, Corinthian columns and domic entrances.

facts.fact: Another storey was added on top of the side blocks in the 1940s.
facts.quote: Another storey was then built on top of the blocks in the 1940s.

facts.fact: Three sculptures of Marianne, the personification of the French Republic, sit in the pediments of the façade.
facts.quote: On the facade of the building, three sculptures of Marianne are placed in the middle of the pediments.

facts.fact: The Saigon Opera House is a municipal opera house in downtown Ho Chi Minh City and an example of French colonial architecture in Vietnam.
facts.quote: Like other French-built opera houses during French colonial period, including the ones in Hanoi and Haiphong, it is an example of French colonial architecture in Vietnam.

facts.fact: Its design is the work of architect Félix Olivier, with construction supervised by Ernest Guichard and Eugène Ferret in 1900.
facts.quote: The Municipal Theatre owes its specific characteristics to the work of architect Félix Olivier, while construction was under supervision of architects Ernest Guichard and Eugène Ferret in 1900.

facts.fact: Its style follows the Flamboyant style of the French Third Republic, with a façade shaped like the Petit Palais in Paris.
facts.quote: Its architectural style is influenced by the Flamboyant style of the French Third Republic, with the façade shaped like the Petit Palais, which was built in the same year in France.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1898 on the site of an earlier theatre and was completed by 1 January 1900.
facts.quote: In 1898, the construction of the new theatre commenced on the site of the old one, and it was completed by 1 January 1900.

facts.fact: It once held 1,800 people on a main floor and two upper levels.
facts.quote: The house had a main seating floor plus two levels of seating above, and once was capable of accommodating 1,800 people.

facts.fact: Some of the façade decoration, criticised as too ornate, was removed in 1943.
facts.quote: Instead, decorations, engravings and statues were removed from the theatre façade in 1943 to make the theatre look newer.

facts.fact: It housed South Vietnam's National Assembly from 1956 until 1967.
facts.quote: The 500-seat building served as the house of the unicameral National Assembly from 1956 until 1967.

facts.fact: The façade was restored in 1998 for Saigon's 300th anniversary.
facts.quote: In 1998, on the occasion of 300th anniversary of the founding of Saigon, the municipal government had the theatre façade restored.

facts.fact: The opera house stands on August Revolution Square in central Hanoi, at the head of Tràng Tiền street.
facts.quote: It is located at August Revolution Square, anchoring the head of Tràng Tiền street.

facts.fact: It was modelled on the Palais Garnier in Paris, but smaller and in materials better suited to the local environment.
facts.quote: One of Hanoi's most prominent architectural landmarks, the Hanoi Opera House was modeled on the Palais Garnier, the older of Paris's two opera houses, but with a smaller scale and using materials that are more suitable to the local environment.

facts.fact: Built in the Neoclassical style with French Renaissance elements, it was first designed by Broyer and Victorin Harlay and completed by François Lagisquet with Harlay.
facts.quote: Built in the Neoclassical style with French Renaissance elements, the design was initially conceived by French architect Broyer and Chief Inspector of Public Buildings Victorin Harlay, and later fully realized by French architect François Lagisquet in collaboration with Harlay.

facts.fact: Construction started in June 1901 and finished in December 1911.
facts.quote: Construction started in June 1901 and finished a decade later in December 1911.

facts.fact: It is one of three opera houses built in colonial French Indochina, with those in Haiphong and Saigon.
facts.quote: Originally built by the French colonial administration as the Hanoi Municipal Theater (French: Théâtre municipal de Hanoï, Vietnamese: Nhà hát Thành phố Hà Nội) between 1901 and 1911, it is one of three opera houses built during the colonial period in French Indochina, alongside the Haiphong Opera House and Saigon Opera House.

facts.fact: The theatre had 870 seats.
facts.quote: However, the 870-seat theater stood mostly empty for the rest of the year, with only the occasional military band or touring soloist making brief appearances.

facts.fact: In September 1945 Viet Minh leaders proclaimed independence from its balcony.
facts.quote: In September 1945, Viet Minh leaders proclaimed the independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam from the Opera House balcony.

facts.fact: A full renovation ran from 1995 to 1997 under French-Vietnamese architect Hồ Thiệu Trị.
facts.quote: The project began in 1995 and was completed two years later, with the participation of 100 workers under the supervision of French-Vietnamese architect Hồ Thiệu Trị, author of the restoration plan.

facts.fact: The museum in Hanoi is about the 54 officially recognised ethnic groups of Vietnam.
facts.quote: The Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (Vietnamese: Bảo tàng Dân tộc học Việt Nam; French: Musée d'ethnographie du Viêt Nam) is a museum in Hanoi, Vietnam, which focuses on the 54 officially recognised ethnic groups in Vietnam.

facts.fact: It sits on a 43,799 m2 site in Cầu Giấy District, about 8 km from the city centre.
facts.quote: It is located on a 43,799-square-metre (10.823-acre) property in the Cầu Giấy District, about 8 km from the city center.

facts.fact: Construction ran from 1987 to 1995 and the museum opened on 12 November 1997.
facts.quote: Construction lasted from 1987 to 1995, and it was opened to the public on 12 November 1997.

facts.fact: The exhibition building, shaped like a Đông Sơn drum, was designed by Ha Duc Linh, a Tày architect; French architect Véronique Dollfus designed the interiors.
facts.quote: The exhibition building was designed by the architect Ha Duc Linh, a member of the Tày ethnic group, in the shape of a Đông Sơn drum, and the interior architecture was designed by the French architect Véronique Dollfus.

facts.fact: A second, kite-shaped exhibition building on Southeast Asian ethnology opened in 2013.
facts.quote: The second exhibition building focusing on Southeast Asian ethnology was designed in a kite shape and was opened in 2013.

facts.fact: The collection holds more than 15,000 artifacts.
facts.quote: The museum's collection comprises more than 15,000 artifacts, 2,190 slides, 42,000 photographs, 237 audiotapes, and 373 videotapes.

facts.fact: Hotel Indonesia in Central Jakarta was one of the first five-star hotels in Southeast Asia and is a city landmark.
facts.quote: Located in Central Jakarta, it was one of the first 5-star hotels in Southeast Asia and remains a major landmark of Jakarta.

facts.fact: It was designed by Danish architect Abel Sorensen and his wife, Wendy Becker.
facts.quote: Occupying 25,082 m2 (269,980 sq ft) of land, the Hotel Indonesia was designed by Danish architect, Abel Sorensen, and his wife, Wendy Becker.

facts.fact: President Sukarno built it for the 1962 Asian Games, to show a modern Indonesia to the world.
facts.quote: The hotel was constructed by Indonesia's first president, Sukarno, in preparation for the 1962 Asian Games, to showcase a modern Indonesia to the world.

facts.fact: It opened for business on 16 July 1962.
facts.quote: The Hotel Indonesia, which was operated by Intercontinental Hotels until 1974, opened for business on July 16, 1962.

facts.fact: It was declared a national cultural heritage site in 1993.
facts.quote: The Hotel Indonesia was declared a national cultural heritage site by the decree of the Governor of DKI Jakarta No. 475 on 29 March 1993.

facts.fact: The hotel has two wings: the 16-storey Ramayana Wing and the 8-storey Ganesha Wing.
facts.quote: The hotel consists of two wings, the 16-story Ramayana Wing and the 8-story Ganesha Wing, including a Presidential Suite and four Diplomatic Suites.

facts.fact: Closed for full renovation in 2004, it reopened on 20 May 2009 as the Hotel Indonesia Kempinski.
facts.quote: In 2004, the government-owned hotel was closed for a complete renovation. It reopened on 20 May 2009 as the Hotel Indonesia Kempinski, managed by Kempinski Hotels under the ownership of Djarum, the oldest luxury hotel group in Europe.

facts.fact: Gedung Sate is a public building in Bandung, West Java.
facts.quote: Gedung Sate is a public building in Bandung, West Java, Indonesia.

facts.fact: Dutch architect J. Gerber designed it in a neoclassical style with native Indonesian, including Hindu-Buddhist, elements, for the colonial department of government enterprises; it was completed in 1924.
facts.quote: It was designed according to a neoclassical design incorporating native Indonesian elements (such as Hindu-Buddhist elements) by Dutch architect J. Gerber to be the seat of the Dutch East Indies department of State Owned Enterprises (Departement van Gouvernmentsbedrijven, literally "Department of Government Industries"); the building was completed in 1924.

facts.fact: Today it is the seat of the governor of West Java and also a museum.
facts.quote: Today, the building serves as the seat of the governor of West Java, and also a museum.

facts.fact: Its nickname means 'satay building', after the central pinnacle shaped like a satay skewer.
facts.quote: Its common name, Gedung sate, is a nickname that translates literally from Indonesian to 'satay building', which is a reference to the shape of the building's central pinnacle - which resemble the shape of one of the Indonesian traditional dish called satay.

facts.fact: The pinnacle's six spheres stand for the six million guilders spent on the building.
facts.quote: The central pinnacle consists of six spheres that represent the six million guilders funded to the construction of the building.

facts.fact: Its roof shows Gerber's attention to local architecture.
facts.quote: Gerber's Gedung Sate shows consideration of local architect in the form of its roof.

facts.fact: The Savoy Homann is a historic hotel on Asia Afrika Street in Bandung, built in 1939 to replace the 19th-century Homann Hotel.
facts.quote: The Hotel Savoy Homann is a historic four-star hotel located on Asia Afrika Street, Bandung, Indonesia. It was built in 1939, replacing the 19th century Homann Hotel.

facts.fact: Designed by Dutch architect Albert Aalbers, it has an Art Deco exterior and interior and is a fine example of Art Deco colonial architecture in the East Indies.
facts.quote: Designed by the Dutch architect Albert Aalbers, the hotel features art deco exterior and interior, and historic furniture. It is an architectural heritage and a fine example of art deco colonial architecture of the East Indies.

facts.fact: In 1939 it was rebuilt in a curved, streamlined Art Deco style.
facts.quote: In 1939, the hotel was rebuilt in a curved streamlined art deco style, designed by the architect Albert Aalbers.

facts.fact: Its exterior is shaped by an 'ocean wave' façade and a vertical central tower, while the interior kept a colonial classical style.
facts.quote: The ocean wave facade and the vertical tower in the middle thus decorate the hotel's exterior, while Aalbers kept the colonial classical style for the interior.

facts.fact: Aalbers' style was inspired by Frank Lloyd Wright and Le Corbusier.
facts.quote: Aalbers' style was inspired by expressionist Frank Lloyd Wright and modernist Le Corbusier.

facts.fact: During the 1955 Asian–African Conference in Bandung it hosted VIP guests.
facts.quote: In 1955, when the first Asian–African Conference was held in Bandung, Savoy Homann hosted VVIP guests and became a part of the Historical Walk.

facts.fact: The hotel has three wings and 185 guest rooms.
facts.quote: The hotel has three wings: the Tower Wing, Garden Wing and Millennium Wing. It has a total of 185 guest rooms.

facts.fact: Jakarta Cathedral, the Church of Our Lady of the Assumption, is the seat of the Archbishop of Jakarta.
facts.quote: Jakarta Cathedral (Indonesian: Gereja Katedral Jakarta; Dutch: Kathedraal van Jakarta) is a Latin Catholic cathedral in Jakarta, Indonesia, which is also the seat of the Archbishop of Jakarta, currently Cardinal Ignatius Suharyo Hardjoatmodjo.

facts.fact: The present cathedral was consecrated in 1901 and built in the neo-Gothic style.
facts.quote: This current cathedral was consecrated in 1901 and built in the neo-Gothic style, a common architectural style to build churches at that time.

facts.fact: The present church was rebuilt between 1891 and 1901, first to designs by Pastor Antonius Dijkmans.
facts.quote: The present church is the structure that was rebuilt between 1891 and 1901. Pastor Antonius Dijkmans, SJ was appointed as the architect.

facts.fact: Marius Hulswit simplified Dijkmans' design so untrained workers could build it, adding cast-iron spires.
facts.quote: Marius Hulswit simplified Dijkmans' design, allowing it to be built by construction workers without practical training. For that reason he added cast-iron spires to the church.

facts.fact: The plan is a cross, 60 m long from narthex to apse.
facts.quote: The plan of the cathedral took the form of a cross. Complete with a narthrex, nave, crossing, transepts, aisles, choir, and an apse on the eastern end. with a length from the narthrex to the apse of 60 meters and 10 meters wide, plus 5 metres on each aisle.

facts.fact: Its two tallest spires, each 60 m, stand on either side of the entrance portal.
facts.quote: There are three main spires in Jakarta Cathedral: the two tallest ones measured 60 metres tall and are located in front on each side of the portal they are collectively known as the narthrex.

facts.fact: The walls are thick red brick, plastered and patterned to look like natural stone.
facts.quote: The body of the building was made of thick red bricks covered with plaster and applied with patterns to mimic natural stone construction.

facts.fact: Iron spire frames and teak roofs were used instead of stone because they are lighter in an earthquake-prone region.
facts.quote: Iron and wood are not suitable as typical neo-Gothic architecture materials usually employ stone masonry. However, these materials were chosen because they are relatively lighter than stone masonry, considering Indonesia is a region that is prone to earthquakes.

facts.fact: The building is Manila's central post office and headquarters of the Philippine Postal Corporation.
facts.quote: The Manila Central Post Office, often referred to as the Post Office Building, is the central post office of Manila and serves as the headquarters of the Philippine Postal Corporation (PHLPost).

facts.fact: Its riverside site on the Pasig was part of the Burnham Plan, which saw the river as a route for carrying mail.
facts.quote: Its location along the Pasig River was part of the Burnham Plan of Manila, which envisioned the river as a convenient route for the transportation of mail.

facts.fact: It was designed by Juan M. Arellano, Tomás Mapúa and Ralph Doane in the neoclassical style.
facts.quote: The original building was designed by Juan M. Arellano, Tomás Mapúa, and Ralph Doane in the neoclassical style.

facts.fact: Considered Arellano's masterpiece, its neoclassical design expresses order and balance.
facts.quote: Considered to be Juan Arellano's magnum opus, it was designed in the neoclassical style that expressed order and balance.

facts.fact: Sixteen Ionic columns line the steps in front of the long rectangular block.
facts.quote: Fronting the huge, rectangular volume are the 16 Ionic pillars that are lined up above the steps just before entering the lobby.

facts.fact: The main body is topped by a recessed attic storey and flanked by two semi-circular wings.
facts.quote: The main body of the building is capped by a recessed rectangular attic storey and flanked and buttressed by two semi-circular wings.

facts.fact: It was rebuilt in 1946, keeping most of its original design.
facts.quote: The building was subsequently rebuilt in 1946, retaining most of its original design.

facts.fact: It was declared an Important Cultural Property in 2018.
facts.quote: In 2018, the National Museum of the Philippines declared the Manila Post Office building as an "important cultural property" (ICP), meaning that it had "exceptional cultural, artistic, and historical significance to the Philippines", allowing it to receive government funding for its protection, conservation and restoration.

facts.fact: A major fire on 21 May 2023 severely damaged the building.
facts.quote: Shortly before midnight on May 21, 2023, the building was severely damaged by a major fire that started in the basement and spread throughout the structure.

facts.fact: The Manila Hotel is a 550-room historic hotel on Manila Bay.
facts.quote: The Manila Hotel is a 550-room, historic five-star hotel located along Manila Bay in Manila, Philippines.

facts.fact: It opened on 4 July 1912, American Independence Day.
facts.quote: It was opened on the commemoration of American Independence on July 4, 1912.

facts.fact: It was built on 35,000 m2 of reclaimed land at the north-western end of Rizal Park.
facts.quote: The hotel complex was built on a reclaimed area of 35,000 square metres (380,000 sq ft) at the northwestern end of Rizal Park along Bonifacio Drive in Ermita.

facts.fact: The original design had an H-shaped plan with well-ventilated rooms on two wings and wide views of the harbour, the Luneta and Intramuros.
facts.quote: The original design was an H-shaped plan that focused on well-ventilated rooms on two wings, providing grand vistas of the harbor, the Luneta, and Intramuros.

facts.fact: The top floor was a large viewing deck.
facts.quote: The top floor was, in fact, a large viewing deck that was used for various functions, including watching the American navy steam into the harbor.

facts.fact: Its penthouse was the home of General Douglas MacArthur from 1935 to 1941.
facts.quote: Its penthouse served as the residence of General Douglas MacArthur during his tenure as the Military Advisor of the Philippine Commonwealth from 1935 to 1941.

facts.fact: A 1975 remodelling by Leandro Locsin and Ildefonso Santos added a high-rise tower behind the original five-storey building.
facts.quote: The hotel was remodeled in 1975 and expanded to 570 rooms with the addition of the high-rise hotel building behind the original five-story structure. The renovations were headed by National Artists for Architecture Leandro Locsin and Ildefonso Santos with Patricia Keller, a partner in the international interior design firm of Dale Keller & Associates.

facts.fact: In the 1975 remodelling, its spartan interiors in a simplified Mission style gave way to more lavish furnishings.
facts.quote: The hotel's spartan interiors in simplified Mission style gave way to more lavish furnishings.

facts.fact: The Main Building is the administrative centre of the University of Santo Tomas in Manila and houses its Museum of Arts and Sciences.
facts.quote: The Main Building of the University of Santo Tomas (UST) in Manila, Philippines functions as the university's administrative center, and home of the Faculty of Civil Law, Faculty of Pharmacy, and the College of Science. The Main Building is also the home of the Museum of Arts and Sciences.

facts.fact: Designed by Fr. Roque Ruaño, it was the first earthquake-resistant building in the Philippines; Ruaño was influenced by Frank Lloyd Wright's Imperial Hotel in Tokyo.
facts.quote: The building, designed by Fr. Roque Ruaño, O.P., is the first earthquake-resistant building in the Philippines. Ruaño was influenced by Frank Lloyd Wright's Imperial Hotel, Tokyo.

facts.fact: The design may have been refined after lessons from the 1923 Great Kantō earthquake; construction began in 1924.
facts.quote: However, some fine tunings may have been made on the design criteria as a result of the new lessons learned from the Great Kantō earthquake of September 1, 1923, which flattened Tokyo and Yokohama. Eventually, construction began in 1924.

facts.fact: The rectangular building measures 86 by 74 m and has two interior courtyards.
facts.quote: The structure is a rectangular building having a dimension of 86 meters long and 74 meters wide with two interior courtyards or patios.

facts.fact: It is made of 40 separate structures, independent of one another.
facts.quote: The most significant feature is the fact that it is actually made up of 40 separate structures independent from one another with the only opportunity provided by pre-cast stab flooring.

facts.fact: The first classes were held on 2 July 1927.
facts.quote: Construction began on 1924 and first classes were held on July 2, 1927.

facts.fact: Statues by Francesco Monti on the fourth-floor pedestals were installed between 1949 and 1953.
facts.quote: Designed by the Italian Francesco Monti, faculty member of the College of Architecture, they were installed between 1949 and 1953.

facts.fact: During World War II the Japanese turned the university into the Santo Tomas Internment Camp.
facts.quote: After the invasion and occupation of the Philippines by the Japanese during World War II, the Japanese converted the university into the Santo Tomas Internment Camp for Americans and other non-Filipinos starting on January 4, 1942.

facts.fact: Manila Cathedral is the Roman Catholic cathedral of the Archdiocese of Manila, dedicated to the Immaculate Conception.
facts.quote: The Minor Basilica and Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, commonly known as the Manila Cathedral, is a Roman Catholic basilica and the cathedral of the Archdiocese of Manila.

facts.fact: The present building is the eighth on the site, completed in 1958.
facts.quote: The original structure dates from 1581, and its eighth re-construction was completed in 1958.

facts.fact: After World War II it was rebuilt under the supervision of Kapampangan architect Fernando Ocampo.
facts.quote: The plan was dropped when the cathedral was reconstructed under Cardinal Rufino Santos, under the supervision of Kapampangan architect Fernando Ocampo.

facts.fact: The first cornerstone was laid on 8 December 1954 and the building was consecrated on 7 December 1958.
facts.quote: The first cornerstone of the eighth cathedral was blessed and laid by Cardinal Fernando Quiroga Palacios, the Archbishop of Santiago de Compostela and papal legate of Pope Pius XII, on December 8, 1954. The building was consecrated on December 7, 1958, and the high altar was consecrated on December 10 that year.

facts.fact: It has a Latin-cross plan, and its Neo-Romanesque façade copies that of the previous cathedral.
